lead: Petrol rose to about N1,430 a litre in Abuja as marketers passed on the Dangote refinery's latest increase and crude stayed above $100. Bamanga Tukur was buried in Yola, and Nigeria used the BRICS summit to call for reform of the UN and global lenders. Gunmen abducted six imams in Zamfara and attacked farmers in Birnin Gwari, an ally of Governor Adeleke was shot dead in Ile-Ife, and the Falconets beat New Caledonia 10-1 to reach the last 16.

items.h: Petrol reaches N1,430 a litre in Abuja
items.s: Filling stations in the FCT raised pump prices to as much as N1,430 after the Dangote refinery's N85 increase to N1,350 at the gantry. Prices in major cities ranged from N1,400 to N1,450 as crude stayed above $100.

items.h: Bamanga Tukur buried in Yola
items.s: Former PDP national chairman Bamanga Tukur was buried in his hometown after Islamic funeral prayers. Vice President Shettima called him a global star.

items.h: Nigeria calls for reform of UN and global lenders at BRICS
items.s: Nigeria's message to the BRICS summit, delivered in President Tinubu's name, called for a more representative UN and an overhaul of international financial institutions. Shettima said Nigeria will not isolate itself from global trade.

items.h: Tinubu moves from UK to Paris on annual leave
items.s: President Tinubu arrived in Paris on Sunday for the second leg of a three-week vacation in Europe.

items.h: Gunmen abduct six imams in Zamfara
items.s: Police and the army confirmed that gunmen kidnapped six imams in Zamfara State, Premium Times reported.

items.h: Bandits attack farmers in Birnin Gwari
items.s: Gunmen raided farmland around Dunya and Shado in Birnin Gwari's Kuyello Ward, killing a number of farmers and wounding or kidnapping others.

items.h: Adeleke ally shot dead in Ile-Ife
items.s: Olalekan Oyeyemi, known as Ajagungbade Emir, was killed by suspected hoodlums on Sunday in a dispute over control of a garage, raising tension in Ile-Ife.

items.h: Falconets beat New Caledonia 10-1 to reach last 16
items.s: Nigeria's under-20 women thrashed New Caledonia in Poland to qualify for the round of 16, where they will face England.

items.h: Eighteen candidates on INEC's final presidential list
items.s: Tinubu, Atiku and Obi are among 18 candidates on INEC's final list. Accord's Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim said no administrative action can remove his candidacy.

items.h: Miyetti Allah says 200,000 cattle lost in Kaduna this year
items.s: The Kaduna chapter of the cattle breeders' association said more than 50 members were killed and over 200,000 cattle lost to banditry, clashes and rustling in 2026.

items.h: Soldiers arrest three after killing of 17-year-old in Plateau
items.s: Troops arrested three suspects after raiding a settlement believed to have been used by attackers who killed a teenager.

items.h: Three slain herders buried in Mangu
items.s: Herders killed near Aloghom, including 18-year-old Garzali Shaibu, were buried in Mangu town.

items.h: NDLEA intercepts synthetic cannabis from the UK hidden in bread
items.s: The NDLEA seized two shipments of 'Colorado' concealed in consolidated cargo from the United Kingdom, some hidden in bread and speakers.

items.h: Atiku says ASUU strike threat exposes subsidy savings claim
items.s: Atiku Abubakar said the lecturers' fresh strike threat undermines the government's case for removing the fuel subsidy.

items.h: Festus Okoye says cyberattacks hit INEC platforms in 2023
items.s: Former INEC commissioner Festus Okoye said the commission faced cyberattacks and problems uploading presidential results during the 2023 election.

items.h: Presidency defers sale of NNPC oil blocks
items.s: ThisDay reported that the Presidency halted Project Delta, a planned sale of oil blocks held by NNPC, ahead of the election.

items.h: Nigeria meets OPEC quota but trails budget output
items.s: Nigeria complied with its OPEC quota for a fourth month in August, but crude production remained below the budget benchmark.

items.h: CPPE urges relief as petrol prices rise
items.s: The Centre for the Promotion of Private Enterprise asked the government to cushion households and businesses from higher fuel costs.

items.h: Uba Sani says women Islamic scholars back Tinubu for his record
items.s: The Kaduna governor said Northern women ulama endorsed the President's re-election because of his achievements and inclusive style.

items.h: Matawalle mobilises Zamfara for Tinubu
items.s: Minister of State for Defence Bello Matawalle urged his supporters in Zamfara to work for the President's re-election.

items.h: Alia tells Ortom to stop distracting him
items.s: Benue Governor Hyacinth Alia said he is focused on rebuilding the state and accused former governor Samuel Ortom of distractions.

items.h: Akwa Ibom governor denies seizing predecessor's house
items.s: Governor Umo Eno denied any rift with former governor Udom Emmanuel and rejected claims that he used the EFCC to take his house.

items.h: ADC says it can beat APC in a free and fair election
items.s: ADC spokesman Bolaji Abdullahi said the party will defeat the APC if the 2027 vote is credible.

items.h: Utomi's Big Tent targets grassroots and vote protection
items.s: Pat Utomi's political group said it will focus on mobilising voters and protecting votes in 2027.

items.h: Group asks Atiku, Obi and Kwankwaso to step aside for Adebayo
items.s: The Forum for Democratic Patriots urged the three opposition figures to drop their ambitions and back the SDP candidate.

items.h: Police deny officers died in checkpoint crash
items.s: A police spokesperson said no officer was killed or injured in the crash, contrary to reports.

items.h: Mowe residents 18 months without power appeal to minister
items.s: A community near Mowe in Obafemi Owode asked the Power Minister and NERC to restore electricity after 18 months.

items.h: Oyo restates commitment to education as schools resume
items.s: The Oyo government outlined its education plans as the 2026/2027 session began on Monday.

items.h: Hausa community in Europe names Gwarzo chancellor
items.s: Professor Adamu Abubakar Gwarzo was appointed chancellor of the Hausa Community in Europe.
